title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a false-positive identification failure at the point where an automated alert becomes a police stop. A license plate camera system flagged a stolen Camaro, an undercover unit saw a car that matched, and the match was treated as sufficient to surround the vehicle with patrol cars and a helicopter and hold its occupants at gunpoint. The system's output was a lead, but it was acted on as an identification.

The gap was in verification, and it was known at the time. Officers and the helicopter could not read the plates on the car, which is the step that would have confirmed or cleared the match before the stop. Running the plates or approaching differently, as one of the men's mothers said afterward, would have caught it. Instead the unreadable plate was carried forward into an armed detention, and the error was discovered only after the men were handcuffed.

What is not established is whether the camera system itself misread anything, whether deputies followed procedure, and whether the account of the threat to shoot is accurate. The sheriff's office has said supervisors will review body worn camera video, and both men plan to file internal affairs complaints. No finding of misconduct and no ruling has been issued.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in a Cypress neighborhood, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two men, both 19, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves. Deputies surrounded their Camaro with at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, pointed guns, and handcuffed them. Julian said a deputy pushed him down and threatened to shoot him, and he showed cuts on his arms. Deputies believed the car was stolen because license plate cameras had flagged a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies. An undercover unit saw a matching car, but officers and the helicopter could not read its plates, so they called backup. After handcuffing the men, deputies realized it was the wrong car.

Anthony's mother, Leslie, wants deputies held accountable and plans to hire an attorney. She said they could have run the plates or approached differently. The Harris County Sheriff's Office said supervisors will review body worn camera video to check whether procedures were followed. The men were given information on filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
